Alright, the user wants the logo to keep that “hand‑drawn” randomness but transition smoothly between frames, as if the drawing is being remembered and slightly altered each time. The previous solution used discrete seed flips, which gave that jittery, flip‑book feel, but the user still perceives jumps. I know that seed values are discrete; you can’t interpolate between them. The way to get a smooth morph while preserving randomness is to keep the same noise texture but pan it over time. By animating the position of the turbulence (using an <feOffset> on the turbulence output), the displacement map will sample different parts of the noise field continuously, giving the illusion of a new random pattern that changes fluidly.

So I need to modify the existing <filter id="logoBoil"> definition. Right now it looks like this (the exact block I captured earlier when editing):

```
<filter id="logoBoil" x="-5%" y="-5%" width="110%" height="110%">
    <feTurbulence type="fractalNoise" baseFrequency="0.0035" numOctaves="1" seed="1" result="noise">
      <animate attributeName="seed" values="1;7;13;4;9;2" dur="0.96s" repeatCount="indefinite" calcMode="discrete"/>
    </feTurbulence>
    <feDisplacementMap in="SourceGraphic" in2="noise" scale="30" xChannelSelector="R" yChannelSelector="G"/>
</filter>
```

I need to replace the <animate seed> with an <feOffset> that animates dx and dy, and remove the seed animation entirely. Also, because the offset will move the noise outside the original filter bounds, I should enlarge the filter region to avoid clipping. Setting x and y to -50% and width/height to 200% should give enough room.

<filter id="logoBoil" x="-50%" y="-50%" width="200%" height="200%">

</filter>
